## Choosing a grid: Cartesian, spherical-polar or cubed sphere (`geometry.type`) {#sec-ch03-choosing}

### Summary

The grid type is the coordinate system the solver integrates on, set by the key `geometry.type` (and on the whole
sphere also by `distribute.layout`). Choosing it is first a matter of the domain: a box, a sector of a spherical
shell, or the whole shell. This section collects, for each of the three working grids, what the code requires, what work it adds to every stage and what it leaves out, so that a
reader can match a grid to a problem. It is a guide to the facts of the other sections of this chapter, not a
recommendation for a study: no section of the report and no test at the pin measures run time per grid type, so the
cost is stated as the work done, not as seconds.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Matches a domain to a grid type, with each grid's requirements, added work and limits (@tbl-ch03-choosing).

**Data.** In: the domain of the problem. Out: the values of `geometry.type` and `distribute.layout`.

**Placement.** Setup: the deck's `geometry` and `distribute` blocks.

**Activation.** `geometry.type`; default `cartesian`. Names other than `cartesian`, `spherical-polar`,
`gnomonic-equiangle` and `cylindrical` are refused.

**Guarantee / limits.** N/A, a guide; no timing per grid is measured at the pin.

**Evidence.** The sections each row cites; the example decks of @tbl-ch03-choosing-code.
:::

Local symbols: $r$, $\theta$, $\varphi$ as in @sec-ch03-sphpolar; $\Delta\theta$, $\Delta\varphi$ [rad] the cell
widths in $x_2$ and $x_3$; $\Delta x_{3,ijk}$ the centre width of cell $(i,j,k)$ in $x_3$, in m;
$c_s$[^rg-00cabad0ec0e] [m s$^{-1}$] the sound speed.

| grid | the domain it covers | what the code requires | added work in every stage | what it does not provide |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cartesian (@sec-ch03-cartesian) | a box, bounds in m | nothing beyond @sec-ch03-globalgrid | none: no geometric source terms | curvature of any kind |
| spherical-polar (@sec-ch03-sphpolar) | a sector of a shell in $r$, $\theta$, $\varphi$ | $x_2$ inside $[0,\pi]$ | the curvature sources | a pole treatment; tests of the $m_2$, $m_3$ curvature terms |
| cubed sphere (@sec-ch03-gnomonic) | the whole shell, six panels | `distribute.layout: cubed-sphere`, `nx2 == nx3`, `interp_order: 2`, $6n_{\mathrm b,2}^2$ blocks | curvature sources, frame changes, edge-ghost interpolation (@sec-ch03-csinterp), seam sync (@sec-ch03-cslrsync) | a fourth-order edge interpolation |

: The three working grids side by side. `cylindrical` is accepted but builds no metric (@sec-ch03-cylindrical).
{#tbl-ch03-choosing}

### Derivation

The one cost that follows from the metric alone is the explicit time step. @sec-ch07-cfl bounds it by the smallest
ratio of a cell's centre width to $\lvert v\rvert+c_s$ in each direction (in $x_1$ unless the vertically implicit
correction replaces that bound). On the spherical-polar grid the
centre width in $x_3$ is

$$
\Delta x_{3,ijk} = r_i\,\lvert\sin\theta_j\rvert\,\Delta\varphi_k ,
$$ {#eq-ch03-choosing-width3}

in m, so a column of cells near a pole has a smaller width, and so a smaller step, than the same $\Delta\varphi$ at
the equator, by the factor $\lvert\sin\theta_j\rvert$ of the cell nearest the pole. In the code,
@eq-ch03-choosing-width3 is `SphericalPolarImpl::center_width3`
({{< code src/coord/spherical_polar.cpp SphericalPolarImpl::center_width3 >}}). On the cubed sphere both horizontal
widths are $r_i$ times a great-circle angle of the panel cell, which has no pole
({{< code src/coord/gnomonic_equiangle.cpp GnomonicEquiangleImpl::center_width3 >}}). This is algebra from the two
widths; the step of a given run was not measured.

### Numerical method

N/A: this section adds no scheme. Each grid's metric is built as its own section describes.

: Code map of the grid choice. {#tbl-ch03-choosing-code}

**How to use it.** Start from an example deck of the chosen grid (@tbl-ch03-choosing-code) and change `geometry`
as @sec-ch03-globalgrid describes. No example deck at the pin uses `spherical-polar`; the grid is set up only by
tests, such as `test_x1_centroid_rest_python` (@sec-ch05-x1cent). Refused: an unknown type ("Unknown coordinate
type"), a spherical-polar $x_2$ range outside $[0,\pi]$, and a cubed sphere with `nx2` $\neq$ `nx3` or
`interp_order` $\neq 2$.

### Tests

N/A: the guide asserts nothing of its own. The tests of each grid are those of @sec-ch03-cartesian,
@sec-ch03-sphpolar and @sec-ch03-gnomonic.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- No run time or memory per grid type is measured at the pin; the cost is stated as work per stage only.
- Spherical-polar has no pole treatment, and its $m_2$ and $m_3$ curvature terms are untested (@sec-ch03-sphpolar).
:::

The table states what the code requires and does, not which grid a study should use. Resolution is chosen with
`geometry.cells` (@sec-ch03-globalgrid); the report gives no guidance on resolution for a given problem.
